Twice a year the sun stands directly over the Ka\'bah at Makkah noon (istiwa\' a\'zam). At that minute, every upright shadow wherever the sun is up points straight away from the Ka\'bah. It is the most exact qibla check there is, with nothing but a stick.

Visible from here, the sun will be {deg}° up. Stand a straight stick upright on level ground and face from the shadow\'s tip to its base. The day before and after also work within about half a degree.
The sun is down here at that moment. Use the daily rashdul qiblat below, or the next Qibla Day.

What the prayer times describe, so you can see them for yourself. For information only, since city lights, haze and buildings hide these signs, and scholars differ on how to read dawn and twilight. Pray by your timetable.
The whole disc of the sun has gone below the horizon and its upper edge has disappeared. Best seen over the sea or open land. Behind hills or buildings it vanishes early, so don\'t pray by that.

The red glow (shafaq ahmar) has gone from the western sky. This is the view of the Shafi\'i, Maliki and Hanbali schools. Imam Abu Hanifah held it is the white glow that follows it. Timetables use the sun\'s depth below the horizon (about 17° to 18°) instead.

True dawn (fajr sadiq) is a thin whiteness spreading sideways along the eastern horizon, growing steadily. It is not the false dawn (fajr kazib) before it, a faint upright column of light that fades again. Researchers still debate the exact depth of the sun at true dawn, so this stays for information only.

Every day shows its source grade. A is official, B is confirmed by a masjid, C is checked by the community, D is calculated. F (falak) marks a reading from your own shadow stick, which only checks the times. In Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia the app downloads the official MUIS, JAKIM or Kemenag timetable for the year (only the year, zone code or regency name is sent) and keeps it in this browser for offline use. If an authority is down, the app\'s own calendar feeds (built weekly from the same tables) stand in. Everywhere else, and before that download, times are calculated in your browser with the country\'s own method, the same engine as the iPhone app, checked against every day of the 2026 MUIS, JAKIM and Kemenag timetables. For Singapore it is never earlier than the official time (at most 2 minutes later). For Malaysia and Indonesia it is within about 2 minutes.

As a traveller you may choose not to fast, and replace the day after Ramadan. If fasting is easy, fasting is better. The day counts as travel when you left home before Fajr. Mark it on your Ramadan page so it is counted for you. Ask your local religious authority when unsure.
Jamak taqdim means praying both in the first prayer\'s time. Jamak ta\'khir means praying both in the second prayer\'s time.
In the Hanafi school the travel distance is about 78 km, for stays of up to 15 days. Prayers are shortened but not joined.
Most of Southeast Asia uses 81 km, which is two marhalah. Some scholars use 89 km. Pick the one your local religious authority uses.
In the Shafi\'i school this holds for stays of up to 3 days, not counting the day you arrive and the day you leave.
This is general guidance on the traveller\'s concessions (rukhsah), not a fatwa. When unsure, follow your local religious authority.

Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura. Online, the app shows MUIS\'s official timetable; offline it calculates, never earlier than the official time.
Malaysia\'s 18° Fajr criterion (since 2019). Online, the app shows JAKIM\'s official e-Solat timetable for your zone; offline it calculates to within about 2 minutes.
Kementerian Agama. Online, the app shows Kemenag\'s official timetable for your city or regency; offline it calculates with offsets fitted on the full 2026 Jakarta, Surabaya and Makassar tables.
The 20°/18° convention used across the Malay world. A sensible default where no national timetable exists.
Standard across Pakistan, India, Bangladesh and Afghanistan.
The official calendar of Saudi Arabia, followed by the Haramain in Makkah and Madinah. Isha is 90 minutes after Maghrib, 120 in Ramadan.
Diyanet\'s method (Fajr 18°, Isha 17°, Asr at one shadow length), with precautionary minutes fitted on its published Istanbul timetable. Used by Turkish masjids across Europe too.
Institute of Geophysics, University of Tehran. Maghrib when the sun is 4.5° below the horizon.
The Egyptian General Authority of Survey. Also common in Syria, Libya and Sudan.
The Islamic Society of North America. Followed by many masjids in the United States and Canada.
Made for northern countries. Fajr and Isha follow the seasons so summer nights stay workable. Common in the UK, Ireland and North America.
The 12° angle used by Musulmans de France (formerly UOIF). Fajr is later and Isha earlier than most methods.
The Spiritual Administration of Muslims of Russia.
The method of Algeria\'s Ministry of Religious Affairs and Endowments.
The method of Tunisia\'s Ministry of Religious Affairs.
The method of Morocco\'s Ministry of Habous and Islamic Affairs.
The method of Jordan\'s Ministry of Awqaf and Islamic Affairs. Also used in Palestine.
